children: Round-up of South Korean financial markets:

** South Korean shares rose on Tuesday as preliminary August trade data showed exports extended strong growth, underpinned by artificial-intelligence demand in the chip sector. The won weakened, while the benchmark bond yield rose. ** The benchmark KOSPI
was up 22.72 points, or 0.33%, at 6,842.74 as of 0104 GMT.  ** Among index heavyweights, chipmaker Samsung Electronics
gained 1.61%. Battery maker LG Energy Solution
climbed nearly 2%. ** Shares of Hyundai Motor
were down 0.87%, while sister automaker Kia Corp

** South Korea's exports surged 68.7% in August from a year earlier, extending their winning streak to a 15th consecutive month and outpacing analysts' forecasts as the economy continued to ride a wave of global technology demand. ** Of the total 901 traded issues, 306 shares advanced, while 540 declined. ** Foreigners were net sellers of shares worth 116.5 billion won. ** The won was quoted at 1,369.2 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform
, 0.09% lower than its previous close at 1,368.0. ** In offshore trading, the won

was quoted at 1,369.7 per dollar, down 0.2% on the day, while in non-deliverable forward trading its one-month contract (KRW1MNDFOR=) was quoted at 1,369.1. ** The KOSPI has climbed 62.37% so far this year. ** The won has strengthened 5.1% against the dollar so far this year. ** In money and debt markets, September futures on three-year treasury bonds (KTBc1) lost 0.10 point to 103.13. ** The most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond yield (KR3YT=RR) rose 4.1 basis points to 3.878%, while the benchmark 10-year yield
